scope: Protected i386 and paged x64 MOV-DR transfers, general-detect faults, accepted #DB GD retirement and original handler retry

path_variables.NEVERD_WORKTREE: NeverD checkout at the recorded base with the recorded changes
path_variables.NEVERC_WORKTREE: NeverC checkout at the recorded commit

integration.qualification: Legacy execution sources, shared register rules and tests are unchanged. Their existing binaries and full P/core runs are retained; final E/core runs use the same binaries. Scheduled-call/export changes require fresh x64 paged, source, export and debug suites on both SDKs; these have separate final run names.

latest_integration.followup: Rebuild both SDKs, repeat debug/execution-breakpoint suites on P and E cores, focused public exports, HighSymSimplify and HighVariableIdentity; compare generated source to the full matrix. Legacy and source suites retain their explicitly recorded earlier build.

contract.binding: Explicit X86InstructionDebugProfile::DebugRegisters with a bound bank. Six architecturally undefined arithmetic flags are preserved, DR6 BLD/RTM are fixed to one, DEBUGCTL is zero; no RTM, bus-lock, BTF, Intel PT breakpoint-trigger tracing, task or data/I/O watchpoint producer is inferred.
contract.owner: X86DebugRegisterEncoding owns raw bytes; X86DebugRegisterRules owns access priority and normalization. Both adapters call the same owner after authenticated original fetch, then existing event/return owners retain faults, backing continuations and restart.
contract.encoding: 0F 21/23, every GPR/debug index and all four ModR/M mod values; mod does not denote memory. One prefix per legacy group and one final REX; 66/67/REX.W do not change transfer width. REX.B selects extended GPRs. LOCK and REX.R remain faulting encodings. Other prefix grammars refuse explicitly.
contract.width: Always 32-bit for protected code16/code32 and 64-bit for long mode. CR4.DE=0 aliases DR4/5 to DR6/7. DR0-3 accept full-width values including noncanonical long-mode addresses.
contract.priority: External eligible events and execution breakpoints retain their existing priority. Original fetch/authentication precede MOV-DR faults. LOCK/REX.R or DE aliases give #UD before CPL #GP; a remaining CPL0 access checks GD before transfer/high-half validation.
contract.writes: DR6/7 high-half writes #GP without bank publication; reserved bits are normalized. A valid DR7 write requesting RTM or unowned comparator controls returns an environment error without inventing #GP or clearing a live control bit.
contract.general_detect: BD is published before entry at the original PC. RF does not suppress GD. The original instruction is incomplete, the incoming SS window is consumed, and accepted #DB clears GD exactly once even across a backing stop. TF/ICEBP/execution-breakpoint #DB also clear GD; software INT 1 does not.
contract.frame_binding: An actual GD cause requires GeneralDetectFrame. FaultResume sets saved RF according to the SDM generic fault rule; ClearResume binds the saved RF=0 observed through this Intel VMX/KVM oracle. Missing/invalid bindings refuse before BD or bank publication. No comparison masks or rewrites the saved frame.
contract.source_compatibility: Paged debug exports requiring an operand callback import neverd_x64_paged_debug_access_v1, preventing an older runtime from interpreting the new DebugRegister operation as a memory request. Ordinary paged exports retain their existing callback. Public export regression checks the new import in both C routes, including ignored mod and faulting encodings.
contract.x64_oracle: Original bytes with KVM guest debugging disabled; all represented GPRs, flags/caches, DR0-3/6/7, shadows and all 256 KiB RAM compared. All registers, aliases, prefixes, mod values, CPL0-3, DE/GD, RF/TF, fetch faults, high halves and reserved bits. Actual handler reads DR7, counts entry, IRETQ and retries the original MOV.
contract.legacy_oracle: Original bytes with guest debugging disabled; represented GPRs/caches/EIP/EFLAGS/CR2, debug bank, shadows/NMI state and all 2 MiB RAM compared. Legacy/PAE paging, independent code/stack/gate widths, CPL0-3, aliases and fault priority. MOV SS itself establishes the SS window; CPL0 first releases lazy VMX MOV-DR interception and sets GD/TF in guest code. Original handler counts entry and IRET retries.
contract.build_matrix: Fork and production r6 SDK; qualified P and E cores; x64 HighC/LLVM-to-C through Clang/NeverC at O0/O2. Full paging, paged execution and source/export regressions are separate recorded runs.

diagnostics_excluded_from_totals.finding: The initial full x64 suites passed, but dev subsequently changed the shared scheduled-call/export path. Its fast-forward integration is recorded separately and all affected x64 suites are rebuilt and repeated; these earlier passes are excluded from final totals.
Fetch-fault setup also unmapped a replaced RSP page; fixed the native fixture to retain a valid handler stack.
Injecting MOV-SS blocking together with TF omitted VMX pending-debug state and caused KVM fail-entry. Original MOV SS now establishes the state, with guest GD/TF setup at CPL0.

Writing DR7 bit 11 retained the RTM control in the CPU but the model cleared it. RTM is now retained through control validation and explicitly refused by this nontransactional profile, with regression checks in both adapters.
Original-only RF/interception probes and passing focused runs are retained as diagnostics and excluded from final totals.

limitations: VMX/KVM can intercept MOV-DR and reinject #DB. The recorded clear saved-RF result does not establish the behavior of unvirtualized general detect; both frame choices remain explicit.

Native qualification is limited to the recorded Intel P/E processors and declared nontransactional profile. Successful DR6/7 reads into the stack register that would prevent handler delivery are checked separately in software.
The KVM CPU lacks LA57; the native five-level paging case is skipped and not counted as a pass.
Data/I/O watchpoints, RTM debug, BTF, bus-lock and task-trap producers, duplicate prefix classes and nonfinal/multiple REX remain outside this profile.
Debug-aware function activation, general i386/compatibility source dispatch, real/VM86/task state, software SMM, SGX/AEX and the other documented machine environments remain unfinished.
LLVM and NeverC native instruction APIs are unchanged. No LLVM release, production SDK pin or LLVM gitlink update is claimed.

The complete regression matrix and latest-dev follow-up are distinct source stages. Full paging/source suites were not repeated for the later HighIR hashing and symbolic-expression integration; the four P/E debug runs and focused public exports were rebuilt on both SDKs. All 216 debug C/manifest files match the full-matrix artifacts exactly.
